theorem.name: FULL_CUT_ANCHOR_VERIFIED_JOIN_TREE_COMPONENT_BOUNDARY_CARRIER
assumptions: B is a canonical variable-only cut discovered by the frozen polynomial min-cut parent and the parent refuses raw conditioning because 2^|B| exceeds its explicit-input budget.
Removing B separates the constraint incidence graph into at least two constraint-bearing components.
For each component C there exists an explicit input relation A_C whose scope contains all variables of B; its B-projections form the only candidate cut-state set S_C.
A deterministic relation tree for C is constructed in polynomial time and independently verified to satisfy running intersection for every variable.
All relations are explicit finite Boolean tables and no semantic relation constraint is dropped.
The downstream contract is exact SAT decision plus one exact witness.
construction: Choose a canonical full-cut anchor relation per component by minimum input-row count with deterministic tie-break.
Project only anchor input rows onto B to form S_C; therefore |S_C| is at most the number of anchor rows and at most the explicit input size.
For each sigma in S_C, restrict each relation by the cut coordinates it contains.
On the verified running-intersection relation tree, perform exact bottom-up/top-down semijoin reduction without materializing the full natural join.
Keep sigma iff all reduced tables remain jointly reconstructible; this forms exact component boundary support P_C.
Intersect all P_C. A nonempty intersection gives a common cut state and one compatible input row per relation; an empty intersection is exact scoped UNSAT.
theorem.soundness: For a relation tree satisfying running intersection, tree-consistent local tuples can be assembled recursively into a global component tuple because every shared variable occurs on the connected path between all relation nodes containing it. Two-pass semijoin pruning removes exactly rows without tree-compatible extensions. Thus sigma is in P_C iff the component natural join has an extension of sigma. Components share only B after the cut, so the whole instance is SAT iff intersection_C P_C is nonempty.
theorem.reconstruction: For an accepted sigma, choose one surviving root row and recursively choose compatible child rows from reduced tables. Running intersection makes assignments path-consistent; merge component witnesses on the common B and disjoint private variables, then replay every original relation table.

complexity.anchor_discovery: Polynomial scan of explicit relation scopes and input row counts.
complexity.candidate_cut_states: At most explicit anchor rows per component, hence O(L); never 2^|B|.
complexity.tree_construction_and_verification: Polynomial maximum-weight spanning-tree construction plus running-intersection graph checks.
complexity.conditional_join: For each anchor state, two tree passes with naive pairwise explicit-row compatibility checks; polynomial in explicit relation-table size.
complexity.carrier_storage: |P_C| <= |S_C| <= anchor input rows <= O(L); global support is a non-expanding set intersection.

claim_ceiling.proves: Exact polynomial boundary-carrier construction for the explicitly frozen overwidth-cut subclass with a raw full-cut anchor in every component and a verified running-intersection relation tree.
does_not_prove: a carrier when no explicit relation exposes all cut variables
a carrier for cyclic/non-running-intersection relation hypergraphs
